thread:
lena-support: FYI customer ACME reporting sudden p99 jump to ~700ms and some 500s for text-generation. They say requests from EU are being served from ap-southeast-1. Trace ID 0x7f9a2c seen in logs.
acme-customer: seeing timeouts around 300-800ms, 5xx about 1-2% of calls since 02:10 UTC. We pinned region eu-west-1 in the SDK config.
sriram-sre: can you paste the trace ID & a curl repro? do you have the raw request headers? @tracebot can you pull the trace 0x7f9a2c?
acme-customer: trace 0x7f9a2c attached (they gave a snippet):
```
trace: 0x7f9a2c
span1: ingress-gw eu-west-1 -> router-01 eu-west-1 (lat 12ms)
span2: router-01 eu-west-1 -> egress-proxy global -> egress-proxy ap-southeast-1 (lat added 420ms)
span3: ap-southeast-1 -> model-host ap-southeast-1 (lat 24ms)
```

lena-support: interesting — router shows an egress-proxy hop to ap-southeast-1. Not expected. Maria, any recent routing policy changes?
maria-runtime: no deliberate change. checking routing policy logs now. Can someone share the exact request headers from the client? need to confirm region hint.
acme-customer: header snippet: `Authorization: Bearer ***`, `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1`, `X-Request-ID: acme-9a3b`, `X-Client-Prefer-Region: eu`
sriram-sre: ok curl repro from our side: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REPRO-TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` returned 502 and trace 0x7f9a2d. attaching logs.
tracebot: pulled traces: 0x7f9a2c, 0x7f9a2d. correlated router logs show a fallback rule matched: `fallback: global` for route `customer:acme` at 02:09:58 UTC. Policy id 0x1b4f.
alex-enginfra: that policy id 0x1b4f was created by a rollback script earlier today that changed default-fallback for customers without dedicated capacity. it incorrectly set `fallback: nearest-available` to `global` in commit b4f9ec. rolling that back now.
jess-ops: rolling back -> staging -> prod? timeline? we need a hotfix to stop new requests matching incorrect fallback.
maria-runtime: pushed immediate patch: router now prefers same-region fallback first; changed evaluation order. polling for metrics.
sriram-sre: replayed same curl after patch: p50 18ms, p99 82ms, no 5xx in 200 calls. trace shows no ap-southeast hop.
acme-customer: we see latency back to normal, thanks. can you share root cause & mitigation?
lena-support: root cause: mistaken rollback/script changed default fallback policy to route to global egress which then preferred ap-southeast-1 for capacity, causing cross-region hops and added ~400ms. mitigation: immediate policy order patch + revert of rollback commit b4f9ec. next steps: (1) postmortem + PR to add test that simulates region hint + fallback matching, (2) add alert when trace shows cross-region egress > 200ms for region-pinned requests, (3) notify customers who had p99 > 300ms during window.
jess-ops: filing incident ticket IN-2026-312, assigning to @alex-enginfra for follow-up and @maria-runtime for observability alerts.
maria-runtime: added a transient guard: if client supplies a region header, router will not fallback to a different continent unless explicit opt-in. will monitor for 30m.
tracebot: incident window 02:09:30-02:11:40 UTC, affected ~0.4% of requests for customers with eu region hints.
lena-support: note for billing: some customers saw retries/timeouts — support to check for duplicate billable tokens; tagging finance in the postmortem.
sriram-sre: thanks team. acme-customer, please reopen if you see further anomalies. :thumbsup:
